$comment: Per-module extra app.<table> names the sql-table-ownership rule permits beyond a
module's own tables (find-sql-table-ownership-violations.ts's ownTables map).
graph: app.visible_people (checked in at
modules/graph/persistence/sql/visible-people.sql) is the canonical authorized-
people CTE (ADR-0004:75-77, C8) and reads app.connections + app.connection_trust
(owned by modules/connections) and app.users (owned by modules/identity) to
produce the projected read model every other consumer must use instead of
joining these tables themselves. This is the one sanctioned exception the rule
exists to police everyone else against — recorded here, not hardcoded, so a
reviewer sees and approves the grant. See find-sql-table-ownership-violations.ts's
docstring and this lane's test-writing report for the open question this
allowlist answers provisionally.
The same grant also covers app.visible_edges (visible-edges.sql), which answers
'which of my visible people know each other' for the graph screen's cluster view.
It reads app.connections for the connection rows themselves and composes
app.visible_people for BOTH endpoints — the double join is what keeps an edge from
ever naming somebody outside the viewer's own authorized set. It deliberately does
NOT read app.connection_trust or app.users: an edge carries two ids and no weight
(ADR-0004 decision 6, ADR-0002 B6), and visible-edges-sql-composition.unit.test.ts
asserts it stays that way. No new table name is granted by adding it.
